## Welcome

This website accompanies the manuscript "*scDiagnostics: systematic assessment of cell type annotation in single-cell transcriptomics data*" (Christidis et al., in review). 

It provides comprehensive tutorials, analysis code, and reproducible workflows demonstrating how [`scDiagnostics`](https://bioconductor.org/packages/scDiagnostics) can evaluate and diagnose automated cell type annotations across different single-cell technologies and biological contexts.

## Overview

We demonstrate `scDiagnostics` across three complementary systems:

**1. Controlled Simulation**
- Synthetic data with known cell types and ground truth
- Controlled introduction of annotation errors
- Validates core diagnostic functions before real data application

**2. COVID-19 PBMC scRNA-seq** (~6,800 query cells)
- Dense, high-cell-count dataset diagnosing annotations from severe COVID-19 infection vs. healthy controls
- Shows how annotation methods handle disease-driven transcriptomic shifts
- Real-world application in infectious disease

**3. MERFISH Mouse Colitis** (~29,000 query cells)
- Spatial transcriptomics dataset evaluating annotations in DSS-induced inflammatory bowel disease (IBD)
- Demonstrates performance on targeted gene panels and spatial information
- Real-world application in chronic inflammation

For each dataset, we generate annotations using four popular tools and compare their performance:

- [**Azimuth**](https://github.com/satijalab/azimuth) — Weighted k-NN mapping
- [**SingleR**](https://bioconductor.org/packages/SingleR) — Correlation-based assignment
- [**CellTypist**](https://www.celltypist.org/) — Machine learning classifier
- [**scVI/scArches**](https://docs.scvi-tools.org/) — Deep learning with VAE
